decline_log.known_gap: RESOLVED as declined-with-reason: the 13 :Problem nodes with no incoming PREREQUISITE_OF edge are now recorded in data/taxonomy/taxonomy_v1.json -> orphan_problems_declined, with the reason (empty technique, coarse topic) and the fix owner (extraction).

orphan_problems_declined.decline_reason: No skill edge added. These 13 :Problem nodes carry an EMPTY technique field and only a coarse topic ('General' x10, 'DI' x3). Since the Q-matrix is now the BKT join spine, deriving a mastery edge from a label that carries no instructional meaning would corrupt mastery signal — worse than the current gap.
orphan_problems_declined.consequence: They remain invisible to BKT: a learner can answer them and no skill updates.
orphan_problems_declined.fix_owner: extraction — needs technique enrichment at source, then edges can be derived.

stub_share.caveat: Prerequisite edges over is_stub skills are structurally valid but semantically thin — the stub skills are harvested placeholders with no topic/sub_topic, not curated taxonomy entries. Consumers should weight closure results accordingly until taxonomy_v1 review lands.
stub_share.note: recomputed after the next_topic retraction: 73.8% (was 61.0%) — removed rows were disproportionately non-stub

key_semantics.warning: template_id is NOT unique across Neo4j labels. All 791 :SolveAlong nodes share their template_id with a distinct :Problem node (verified 2026-09-03), so a label-agnostic MATCH on template_id can resolve to the wrong node.
key_semantics.rule: Always qualify the label when joining on template_id. :Problem and :SolveAlong are separate nodes and are never dual-labeled, so an id-keyed write to one does NOT touch the other.
key_semantics.this_artifact: problem_requirements.template_id means a :Problem node SPECIFICALLY — the rows are derived from (:Skill)-[:PREREQUISITE_OF]->(:Problem) edges. It must not be resolved against :SolveAlong.
key_semantics.consequence: This table is the BKT join spine, so a label-agnostic resolution would attribute mastery to the wrong content.

next_topic_tier_retraction.what: The next_topic-derived tier (82 edges) was retracted from the DAG, the live graph and the promoted closure.
next_topic_tier_retraction.why: NEXT_TOPIC is a browse ring that wraps back to its parent topic, not a pedagogical ordering. Its chains terminate at root skills (Sequences and Series -> Binomial Theorem -> Algebra), so inverting them asserted a sub-topic as the prerequisite of its own root — for all 9 roots. It also supplied 21 of the 23 hops in the longest chain, presenting a table of contents as prerequisite depth.
next_topic_tier_retraction.found_by: coordinator, by rendering the graph as an atlas — invisible in aggregate counts, unmissable once drawn
my_own_gaps: a root guard existed but ran only on the chain_derived tier, so these bypassed it; it now runs on every derived tier
live_load only ADDED edges, so a tier retracted in the builder stayed live and kept feeding the closure; it now reconciles and prunes
